comment: Paths inside a WSL 2 distribution that commonly hold reclaimable data, used by `wslkit disk usage`. This is a catalogue for reporting only: wslkit never deletes anything here. `safe` false does not mean dangerous, it means wslkit cannot judge on the user's behalf. A path starting ~/ is expanded against every real home directory. No entry may end in a slash: the containment check that stops /var/log claiming /var/logbook depends on it.

caches.label: apt package cache
caches.note: downloaded .deb files; apt-get clean empties it and apt refetches on demand

caches.label: pacman package cache
caches.note: paccache -r keeps the most recent versions

caches.label: pnpm store
caches.note: pnpm hard-links from here into every project, so emptying it breaks installed dependencies until they are reinstalled

caches.label: cargo registry
caches.note: sources and .crate files, refetched on the next build

caches.label: rustup toolchains
caches.note: these are installed compilers, not a cache; remove individual ones with rustup toolchain uninstall

caches.label: go module cache
caches.note: go clean -modcache empties it; modules are refetched on the next build

caches.label: maven repository
caches.note: refetched from the configured repositories, which is slow on a poor connection

caches.label: user cache
caches.note: contains the entries above that live under it; the total counts them once

caches.label: docker storage
caches.note: images, containers and volumes, not a cache; reclaim with docker system prune

caches.label: snap packages
caches.note: installed snaps and their old revisions

caches.label: logs
caches.note: includes the journal above; some of it may be wanted evidence

caches.label: temporary files that survive a reboot
